summary: Follow-up on the April 1 outage where Nova Health experienced a ~6 minute latency spike and partial failures on the Redwood hosted inference path. Discussed root cause hypotheses (eviction during autoscaling, KV cache cold starts, network flapping to region), proposed mitigations (instance pinning, aggressive KV prewarm, canary routing to dedicated pool), and agreed next steps for benchmarks and privacy/deployment reviews.
topics: Incident timeline and root cause hypotheses
KV cache cold-start and cache warming strategies
Private deployment vs Dedicated capacity tradeoffs
Security controls: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML concerns
transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-04-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood CSM); Maya Singh (Nova SRE), Daniel Park (Nova CTO), Olivia Chen (Nova Cloud Ops), Priya Rao (Nova Security), Ethan Liu (Product)

Summary: quick sync to align on postmortem findings and confirm mitigations, benchmarks, and timeline for private/dedicated options.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: okay everyone, thank you for joining, uh we'll kick off, Samir and I pulled together the draft postmortem and some proposed mitigations. Maya thanks for taking the lead on the logs.

[00:18] Maya Singh: yeah thanks, um we uploaded the initial syslogs and some traces to the shared folder, I think there's one link in the meeting invite, let me know if anyone can't access it. There's also a pcap for the 02:00 window, could be noisy.

[00:34] Samir Patel: got it, I pulled those down this morning. Quick recap from Redwood side: our telemetry shows a burst of requests at 02:01 UTC, some backpressure in the serving layer, autoscaler triggered new nodes, and a subset of requests saw KV cache misses which increased latency. At the same time we see a couple of host evictions in the cluster that correlate with the error spikes.

[01:02] Daniel Park: when you say eviction, is that preemptible instances getting reclaimed? Or our billing plan had something like spot instances? We thought dedicated pool was in effect for the hot path.

[01:18] Samir Patel: good question. For Nova you have a hybrid config — most traffic is on hosted capacity with a small dedicated fallback pool. The instantiated worker nodes that served the sudden burst were in the hosted pool; some of those were preemptible-ish on the cloud provider side. We saw two evictions during the timeline which caused reconnection and cold KV cache.

[01:44] Olivia Chen: hmm we definitely didn't expect preemptions for those. We had annotated the job config as "high priority" but might have not pinned the instance type; I'll double check with infra.

[02:02] Priya Rao: from security POV we care about audit logs for the node restarts and any KMS key access during the window. We also want to make sure no tokens were leaked during the reconnect.

[02:18] Jordan Reyes: noted, Redwood's postmortem includes the audit logs we captured. Lena, do we have KMS access logs for the timeframe?

[02:28] Lena Ortiz: yes we pulled the KMS audit events and included a redacted snippet in the doc but we'll share full logs with Nova under the NDA. There were no anomalous key usage patterns.

[02:44] Ethan Liu: can we dig into the KV cache behavior — what does 'cold start' mean here? We saw a jump from 80ms to 900ms for a subset of tokens.

[03:02] Samir Patel: right, so our runtime keeps a per-session KV cache to avoid recomputing keys for recent context. When a new node handles a request that wasn't hot for it, it needs to rehydrate the KV from the prefix or from the model state — that adds overhead. In the burst the mix of traffic plus evicted nodes meant many sessions hit cold caches. Also the autoscaler brought up new workers that weren't warmed.

[03:36] Maya Singh: is that something you can prewarm? We have some steady baseline traffic that could be used to warm a small pool.

[03:48] Samir Patel: absolutely, prewarm is an option — we can keep a warm standby pool and proactively replicate active session prefixes. We also recommend intelligent routing: route critical traffic to your dedicated pool where instance pinning is guaranteed, and use hosted for overflow.

[04:08] Daniel Park: what about cost tradeoffs? Keeping a standby pinned pool increases cost. We need a proposal with estimated delta.

[04:18] Lena Ortiz: agreed — we'll include cost delta estimates. As a starting point, Samir can run a simulated workload with your sample traces and produce a cost vs latency matrix for a few configs (hosted-only, hosted+warm-standby, dedicated primary).

[04:36] Samir Patel: yes I'll do that. Also a short-term mitigation is to increase our autoscaler cooldown so we don't churn nodes too fast, and bump prefetch for KV to reduce misses.

[04:50] Maya Singh: the autoscaler cooldown — is that Redwood-managed or do we adjust our request shaping? We had surges from a cron job that might be the root cause.

[05:04] Samir Patel: there's a combination: the platform autoscaler is Redwood-managed but we can tune thresholds per-customer. If it's a cron spike, we can set rate-limiters or queueing on your side. We can also set a temporary soft-limit on scale-down.

[05:22] Olivia Chen: on the network side the pcap shows a few retransmits around 02:02 — could be provider-level network flapping. If the instance got a NIC reset at the same time, that would explain reconnects and the observed latency. We're going to ask our cloud PS team to check provider incident history.

[05:40] Lena Ortiz: good. I want to call out two root cause hypotheses in the doc: (A) autoscaler churn + preemptible eviction -> KV cold-starts; (B) transient network flapping compounded by reconnections causing more cold starts. The mitigation matrix maps to those.

[06:00] Daniel Park: makes sense. One question about dedicated: can we do a staged roll — keep most traffic on hosted but failover to dedicated only when latency crosses threshold?

[06:12] Samir Patel: yes, we support policy-based routing — you can set SLO thresholds and have automatic failover to dedicated pool. There's also canary routing so we can route a small percentage to dedicated to validate.

[06:30] Priya Rao: security question: if we move to dedicated or private deployment, will the KMS integration change? We need to maintain centralized key management.

[06:40] Lena Ortiz: for Redwood Private deployments you can bring-your-own KMS/HSM and we support external key wraps. For Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS via workload identity and we provide audit logs. We'll share the KMS integration guide.

[06:58] Ethan Liu: on the timeline — what's realistic to get the standby warmed and run the benchmarks?

[07:06] Samir Patel: I can run the KV-cache prewarm benchmark using Nova sample traffic and send results within a week — so by 2026-04-20. That will include latency distributions and a cost estimate for a warm standby pool.

[07:20] Maya Singh: good. Also we want to validate failure modes: what happens if the dedicated pool goes unhealthy — do you have graceful degradation?

[07:30] Jordan Reyes: yes, we have fallback policies: roll back to a compatible model variant or route to a hosted pool in another region, and we can configure circuit breakers. We'll include recommended policy settings in the doc.

[07:48] Olivia Chen: any changes we should expect to our integration — SDK changes or config flags?

[07:56] Samir Patel: mostly config flags: instance_pinning=true, prewarm_pool_size=N, routing_policy=canary/threshold. No SDK change needed. We will provide CLI snippets and terraform examples for private/dedicated toggles.

[08:12] Daniel Park: about observability — we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns for last 30 days for our PMs and finance. You mentioned Redwood Console has that. Can we get one-off exports?

[08:26] Lena Ortiz: yes, Redwood Console can export token-level billing and latency. I'll request an export for Nova covering March-April and share a spreadsheet link.

[08:38] Maya Singh: and for compliance, Priya needs the SOC2 artifacts and encryption in transit documentation.

[08:46] Priya Rao: and also RBAC mappings — we need to ensure our operators have the right roles if we try a private deployment.

[08:54] Lena Ortiz: we'll include SOC2/ISO docs and an RBAC mapping guide.

[09:02] Ethan Liu: one minor note — in the doc there was a typo where it said "KV cache miss spike at 0201Z" but the trace shows 02:01:12. Could we correct that for the timeline?

[09:10] Samir Patel: yes we'll tighten timestamps and add the host IDs so it's crystal clear.

[09:18] Maya Singh: another ask: can Redwood simulate a sustained vs spiky load so we can see how autoscaler reacts? We want to tune thresholds.

[09:26] Samir Patel: we can run two tests: ramp (sustained) and burst (spiky) using your sample traces. We'll include telemetry for scale events and KV miss rates.

[09:36] Daniel Park: what's the proposed longer-term reliability improvement? Are we thinking private for PHI workloads?

[09:44] Lena Ortiz: for PHI, many customers prefer Private deployment; that eliminates hosted evictions and gives you more control over networking. Alternatively Dedicated with instance pinning plus warm prewarmed pool might be sufficient if you want faster time-to-value and lower ops overhead. We'll map recommendations to risk tolerances.

[09:58] Priya Rao: does Private support air-gapped on-prem? We have some regs for a subset of workloads.

[10:04] Samir Patel: yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem packaging; that's a heavier lift and includes installation/ops support. We'll scope that separately if you want to pursue.

[10:14] Jordan Reyes: summarizing next steps: Lena will share final postmortem and KMS/audit docs; Maya will provide logs; Samir will run benchmarks; Jordan and Olivia to schedule private/dedicated deep dive. Any objections?

[10:30] Daniel Park: none. Sounds good.

[10:36] Lena Ortiz: great, we'll get those items out. Thanks everyone.

[10:42] Maya Singh: thanks all.

(Notes: references in chat to shared folder: https://redwood.shares/nova-postmortem (placeholder); benchmarking spreadsheet: https://redwood.sheets/nova-bench-2026 (placeholder). Transcript has some automatic speaker mislabels and intermittent transcription errors like "KV cache" transcribed as "KV cash" in a few places; cleaned in the shared doc.)
